text:
maria: Pushed the PRD draft for the Dashboard + Tracing + Retention rollout. Link: https://docs.internal/redwood/prd/dashboard-tracing-retention-v1 — need quick read + callouts on launch criteria and risky edge cases.

arjun: skimmed. high level looks good. can we tighten acceptance criteria around sampling and cost guardrails?

lindsey: UX note — we need a compact 'alerts' funnel in the left-nav for multi-tenant so ops can jump to noisy customers. will attach mock. :spiral_note_pad:

sam: SRE concern: retention tiers currently explode token storage for bursty customers. need a hard cap at ingestion side + graceful truncation policy.

maria: Agreed. Draft AC I added: 
- retention-tiering supports 7d/30d/90d tiers per-org
- per-org ingestion caps enforced at API gateway (configurable)
- when cap reached, oldest traces dropped and an event emitted to metrics.

kevin: small nit: how do we signal dropped traces to customers? email? console banner? event stream?

arjun: console banner + per-org telemetry event + webhook callback. fallback: notify usage owners via email for premium tiers.

maria: Adding acceptance criteria block in PRD: 
```
Acceptance criteria (v1):
1) Dashboards: default TL;DR overview card, 3 pre-built views (latency, error-rate, cost-by-model).
2) Tracing: sample rate configurable per-route, default 1% global, adjustable to 100% for canaries.
3) Retention: 3 tiers (7/30/90), with archival export to S3 for >90d.
4) Ingestion cap: per-org token/sec, enforced at gateway; when exceeded, 429 returned and metric emitted.
5) Rollout: feature flag + 1% canary, 10% ramp, 100% if error budget OK.
```

lindsey: UX acceptance: each dashboard should have a 'save as view' action, and a compact mobile layout for PMs. Also, add affordance for 'view raw trace' on hover.

sam: Edge-case: cross-tenant trace leakage — ensure trace IDs are namespaced by org and never indexed across org indices. add AC: index prefix = org_id_.

arjun: Implementation note: will add a middleware to prefix trace ids and enforce index ACLs. cost estimate: ~2 dev-sprints + 1 qa.

maria: Can we define launch KPIs? Suggested: P50 latency on dashboard queries <400ms (90th perc <1.2s), 0 dropped requests in canary window, retention storage growth <12% of baseline for first month.

kevin: Add metric: number of retention-triggered exports per org <= 5/day for non-enterprise during canary.

maria: Good. Who owns rollout runbook? sam + arjun?

sam: yes. i'll draft runbook steps: monitor pipeline lag, sampling rate, storage delta, error budget, and feature-flag rollback plan.

arjun: I'll scope the backend changes and produce a migration plan for existing customers (auto-migrate free-tier to 7d unless they opt-in).

lindsey: I can produce the console flows and banners. will mock the per-org banner for dropped data.

maria: Ok blockers: (1) confirm archival S3 policies and costs with finance, (2) gating for privacy-sensitive tenants (some need no external archival), (3) automated tests for index isolation.

kevin: FYI deploy-bot scheduled canary window tomorrow 08:00 PT. deploy-bot: canary preflight checks will run on deploy. :robot_face:

deploy-bot: preflight: bucket-write-check OK, index-ACL-lint OK, feature-flag toggles configured.

maria: Next steps: arjun & sam produce runbook + infra PR by EOD Thursday, lindsey deliver mocks by Wed EOD, finance note on archival costs from kevin by Friday. I'll update PRD with these ACs and call the sync after mocks are in. :thumbsup:

arjun: noted. I'll also add a small snippet for the gateway config for per-org caps: 
```
POST /gateway/config
{
  "org_id": "<org>",
  "rate_limit_tokens_per_sec": 500,
  "on_overflow": "emit_metric_and_429"
}
```

sam: will add automated alert: if per-org 429s > 0.1% of requests for 5m during canary, auto-rollback.

maria: Great. thanks all — will ping when PRD updated. :rocket:
